question.text: A metal <math><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi></math> forms the sulphate <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mfenced></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>.</mo></math> A <math><mn>0.596</mn></math> gram sample of the sulphate reacts with excess <math><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> to give <math><mn>1.220</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><mo>.</mo></math> What is the atomic weight of <math> <mtext>M</mtext>  </math>(in g/mol)?

solution.text:
Mole of BaSO4=1.22233.3
Moles of M2SO43=1.22233.3×13
=1.743×10-3
Wt. of M2SO43=0.596
∴  1.743×10-3 2M+96×3=0.596
M=26.9
